samples.question: The framed box at the top of this image shows a reference shape. A thick horizontal line separates that box from a row of four panels, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right and separated by thick vertical lines. Each panel holds one solid shape drawn at its own arbitrary rotation. Exactly one panel holds the same shape as the reference, turned in the plane only, so it could be slid and rotated onto the reference without ever being flipped over. Exactly one other panel holds the mirror image of the reference shape, which can only be brought onto the reference by flipping it over; the two remaining panels hold shapes that are neither. The reference is drawn slightly smaller than the panel shapes, so only its form matters, not its size. Every shape in the image has the same colour, and the four panel shapes have the same size, the same area and the same amount of ink, so colour, size, ink and panel position carry no information about the answer. Does the rotated, un-flipped copy of the reference shape lie in the left half of the row (panels 1 and 2) or the right half (panels 3 and 4)? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.
